evidence:
Assembled source joins iPhone data-flow fc55bc7e9 with staging 37e1c2c8f. Native build floor remains 1 and the reviewed contract hash is unchanged. Notification context, reply metadata and nullable delivery columns are additive; ordinary tap routes, server_url and preference shapes remain compatible. Dispatch retains saved context and staging current-task eligibility checks. A no-op migration joins notification_message_context and merge_home_staging_compaction. Native Ticket/navigation decoding retains staging recap freshness fields. Compact conversation previews now decode optional sender attribution and owner-message preview from existing server status facts, only under current authority, while retaining local unsent delivery precedence and excluding transcript admission.

Verification: native unit suite completed 216 tests with 1 expected skip and zero failures. Supplemental diagnostic collection was interrupted after tests completed. The final host suite passed 176 tests, including the remote-refusal regression; 17 system host cases also passed. Fifteen local UI scenarios passed across recorded source pins. The final unsigned Release Simulator build passed on 953fae9ed. These results cover local source and fixture contracts. Full Linux server confirmation remains a separate gate. Exact pins, reruns and diagnostic limits are in the Ticket evidence. An oldest supported signed build, physical iPhone behavior, Apple notification delivery and account distribution remain unproved. No production deployment or next phone build is claimed by this compatibility review.

Recovery admission review: changes to the startup server and deploy interruption coordinator alter retry timing and update admission. They do not change native routes, request headers, response schemas, build policy, or recovery prompt contents. The supported build floor remains 1. The recovery integration suite and focused recovery tests passed. The iOS build gate unit and integration tests passed on Linux. This source review does not prove signed-device behavior; native reads, actions, conversation output, reconnect, unsupported-build handling, and draft retention on the oldest signed build remain release checks.

Worker cleanup review after merge with staging 037dc21386910b351541ba16fc7f5141115cd2f0: Reviewed Worker cgroup cleanup changes against staging 7a835e0b32b55be8da78ad2eeeaeb747ddcc4415. Changed backend files cover Linux launch, process ownership, cleanup and executor service serialization. No HTTP route, request field, response field, event shape, database schema, iOS source or build policy changes. CleanupResult retains complete/reason/scope with the same types; scope text now describes cgroup custody. ConversationAPI.interruptConversation still POSTs /api/conversation/conversations/{id}/interrupt and accepts the existing 204 response from conversation/api.py. Unsupported Linux cleanup retains the existing uncertainty path and fence, without a new native enum or decoding requirement. MINIMUM_SUPPORTED_BUILD remains 1. Verification: 25 existing Python compatibility/build-gate/stop-recovery tests passed; prior focused supervision/backend suite passed 37 tests with zero skips and executor installation passed five. This source review establishes unchanged native wire contracts; physical iPhone behavior and signed-device delivery were not tested on this Linux host. Native CI checks run on the refreshed PR. Recovery admission changes only retry scheduling and workspace admission, while Worker cleanup controls process retirement. Their sources do not overlap and neither changes native wire contracts.

Mac credential handover review: the change moves the original Mac's handover closure to the executor update-report route and makes the Mac executor ask for its credential at each start. It changes only executor routes and the Mac executor client. The iPhone app reads /api/executor/health alone, and that route, its response schema, native request headers, and build policy are unchanged. The supported build floor remains 1. The credential handover unit tests, the full unit suite, and the executor integration tests passed on Linux. This source review does not prove signed-device behavior.

Publish repair review: the only backend change splits one string literal in conversation/backend_state.py across two lines for the line-length lint rule. The model refusal text is identical, and no route, field, schema, event shape or build policy changes. The supported build floor remains 1. The check script and the ruff and mypy checks pass on Linux. This source review does not prove signed-device behavior. The Mac credential handover change (t_xwkw9uw5) moves the old-authority closure from the executor update-report route to a new credentialed POST /api/executor/credential/handover/close, used only by Mac and Linux executor runtimes. The iPhone app reads only /api/executor/health (checked by grep over ios/**/*.swift), whose shape is unchanged, so native builds from 1 remain compatible.

Worker memory notice review on 5873cef49: Compaction boundaries and automatic worker notice scheduling change; no native route, request, response schema, build policy, or event kind changes. A wake can now be followed by a separate Panels-authored prompt using the existing prompt event shape; native conversation rows already accept senderLabel and prompt events. The oldest supported build remains 1. On Linux, the iOS build-gate, compatibility-review, conversation API and conversation-view API unit tests passed, as did the iOS build-gate integration test and the focused conversation, memory and migration suite. These are source and server tests; the oldest signed build, physical iPhone behavior, reads, actions, conversation output, reconnect and draft retention remain device release checks.

Mac Ticket workspace selection review (t_vt4q5rs7): changed only native executor repository selection and shared filesystem discovery. No HTTP route, request/response shape, event kind, database schema, executor protocol shape, iOS source or minimum build policy changed; native build floor remains 1. Both managed native-start regression cases reach the existing scripted backend, and targeted mypy and Ruff passed. This source review does not establish signed-device behavior or claim a production deployment.

Proposal revision CLI review (t_k5gk3b4v): Backend source changes only the CLI argument selection: revise now requires --message or --body-file, with explicit - for stdin. The existing reject HTTP endpoint, body, revision pinning, response, and native build policy remain unchanged. The iOS ReviewAPI sends its own HTTP reject request with message and expectedProposalRevision and does not invoke the CLI. The oldest supported build remains 1. Three focused proposal revision tests passed on Linux, including CLI guidance and native/web stale decision handling. This source review does not establish behavior on the oldest signed build or a physical iPhone.

Extra-machine proposal send-back review: Independent source review confirms that the shared reject writer only extracts the existing HTTP handler body. The route, message and expectedProposalRevision fields, revision parser, resolver and Ticket response serializer remain unchanged. Native ReviewAPI.returnReview keeps the same request. The new capability read is inside authenticated executor transport; native executor health remains unchanged. IPC mapping, receipt retry behavior and executor authority checks do not change native contracts. The oldest supported build remains 1. Existing implementation verification passed 22 canonical decision tests, 31 executor unit cases and the connected executor harness. This source review does not establish physical-device or signed-build behavior.

Worker stop custody review: Linux legacy cleanup now retains its existing uncertainty fence when descendant custody is unproven. Worker scratch isolates default tmux and screen sockets. No native route, response schema, event shape, or minimum build policy changes. The Stop action can report the existing retry error for unproven legacy cleanup. A delegated Linux test verified isolated terminal servers and cleanup. The legacy recovery test verified the fence. This source review does not establish signed-device behavior.

Queued decision delivery review (t_wx94chdk): The change only reconciles backend decision delivery against existing conversation ownership and recorded outcomes. The native approval and return endpoints, request and receipt shapes, conversation event kinds and payloads, and minimum build policy are unchanged. Existing native builds can continue to decode the same data; the supported build floor remains 1. Focused decision-delivery tests passed on Linux. This source review does not establish signed-device or physical iPhone behavior.

Ticket checkout isolation and cleanup review: The backend changes prepare independent Ticket clones, retire eligible checkouts using Worker custody and origin evidence, preserve separate artifacts for seven days, and adjust cleanup scheduling and diagnostics. Mac executor polling and startup identity change inside the existing executor transport. No native HTTP or SSE route, native request or response schema, conversation event kind, or minimum supported build changes. Native artifact access remains on the existing separate Ticket files surface; files inside the checkout are not exposed through it. The supported build floor remains 1. This source review does not prove physical iPhone or oldest signed-build behavior, reads, actions, conversation output, reconnect, or draft retention; those remain release checks. On Linux, targeted Ruff and mypy passed on the combined branch. The full unit suite and executor integration check are separate integration gates.

Consequences completion review (t_7bxkzuq6): Consequences reports now settle automatically; final decision approval accepts omitted onward ceiling and holder. Existing supplied final-boundary choices normalize to completion, while earlier review gates retain their requirements. Native Ticket and Review requests omit those fields only at final approval. Removed waiting_to_closeout is optional in the prior native model. Removed navigation group requests normalize to empty and discard their old cursor, retaining request compatibility. Routes, projection and wire versions, headers, protected receipt identities, conversation transport, and MINIMUM_SUPPORTED_BUILD remain unchanged. Linux focused tests cover canonical final approval, report settlement, migration prompt recovery and navigation compatibility. Native macOS host tests and unsigned Simulator build run on the PR. No signed-device, oldest TestFlight build, physical phone, or production deployment evidence is claimed here.

Mac cleanup refresh ordering review (t_u5jvx73x): The backend diff serializes Mac cleanup refresh capture and publication; it changes no native HTTP or SSE route, response schema, event kind, executor health contract, or minimum build policy. iOS reads executor health via the existing /api/executor/health endpoint. The supported build floor remains 1. This source review does not establish signed-build or physical iPhone behavior; device release checks remain required.

Combined source review: Consequences completion changes Ticket decisions, navigation and native presentation; Mac cleanup refresh ordering changes only the executor reconciliation path. The changes do not overlap and preserve the reviewed native build floor and existing executor health contract. This source review does not replace signed-device release checks.
